records.label: 8-month-old girl

variants.as_reported: de novo balanced translocation between a chromosome 1 and 22

quotes: An eight month old girl was born with symmetrical bilateral oblique facial clefts and calcaneovarus foot deformity. CT scan of the head showed severe bilateral ocular hypoplasia and normal brain parenchyma.
Peripheral blood karyotype showed a de novo balanced translocation between a chromosome 1 and 22.

records.label: 4 Brazilian patients with oblique facial clefts
quotes: Here we report on 4 patients with oblique facial clefts and a strikingly similar facial appearance.
the presence of consanguinity in 3 of them

notes.statement: Saadi et al. (2011) showed that loss-of-function mutations in SPECC1L are pathogenic for oblique facial clefts (ObFC), a unique class of human facial malformations.
quotes: We show that loss-of-function mutations in SPECC1L are pathogenic for this human developmental disorder and that SPECC1L is a critical organizer of vertebrate facial morphogenesis.

notes.statement: Saadi et al. (2011) found that during murine embryogenesis Specc1l is expressed in cell populations of the developing facial primordia, which proliferate and fuse to form the face.
quotes: During murine embryogenesis, Specc1l is expressed in cell populations of the developing facial primordial, which proliferate and fuse to form the face.

notes.statement: Saadi et al. (2011) found that knockdown of a SPECC1L homolog in zebrafish produced a faceless phenotype with loss of jaw and facial structures.
quotes: In zebrafish, knockdown of a SPECC1L homolog produces a faceless phenotype with loss of jaw and facial structures

notes.statement: Saadi et al. (2011) found that knockdown of the SPECC1L homolog in Drosophila phenocopied mutants in the integrin signaling pathway, which exhibit cell-migration and -adhesion defects.
quotes: knockdown in Drosophila phenocopies mutants in the integrin signaling pathway that exhibit cell-migration and -adhesion defects

notes.statement: Saadi et al. (2011) found that in mammalian cells SPECC1L colocalized with both tubulin and actin, and SPECC1L deficiency resulted in defective actin-cytoskeleton reorganization and abnormal cell adhesion and migration. They concluded that SPECC1L functions in actin-cytoskeleton reorganization and is required for proper facial morphogenesis.
quotes: in mammalian cells, SPECC1L colocalizes with both tubulin and actin, and its deficiency results in defective actin-cytoskeleton reorganization, as well as abnormal cell adhesion and migration
SPECC1L functions in actin-cytoskeleton reorganization and is required for proper facial morphogenesis

notes.statement: Richieri-Costa and Gorlin (1994) suggested that the pattern of facial involvement, consanguinity in 3 of their 4 patients, and the overall clinical picture pointed to a unique dysmorphogenetic process. They proposed that in some cases this could represent an oculomaxillofacial dysostosis.
quotes: The pattern of facial involvement, the presence of consanguinity in 3 of them, as well as the entire clinical picture, suggest a unique dysmorphogenetic process which could represent, in some instances, an oculomaxillofacial dysostosis.

notes.statement: Richieri-Costa and Gorlin (1994) noted that oblique facial clefts are rare and include types 2 through 6 of Tessier's classification.
quotes: Oblique facial clefts are rare and include types 2-6 of Tessier's classification.

notes.statement: Dasouki et al. (1988) found a de novo balanced translocation between chromosomes 1 and 22 in a girl with bilateral oblique facial clefts, and stated that a submicroscopic imbalance resulting from the translocation could not be ruled out. They recommended chromosome studies in children with such rare malformations.
quotes: A submicroscopic imbalance secondary to this translocation cannot be ruled out.
Chromosomal studies should be performed in children with such rare malformations.

notes.statement: Dasouki et al. (1988) suggested that the pattern of anomalies would help to tell oblique facial clefts apart from amniotic band disruption.
quotes: The pattern of the observed anomalies will help distinguish between oblique facial clefts and amniotic band disruption.

notes.statement: Tessier (1976) proposed a new anatomical classification of facial, craniofacial, and laterofacial clefts based on personal observations, using the orbit as the primary structure of reference and differentiating 15 locations for clefts, whose courses through soft tissue and bone were described in detail.
quotes: Based on personal observations a new classification of facial, cranio-facial and latero-facial clefts is proposed. The orbit is used as the primary structure of reference. Fifteen locations for clefts can be differentiated.

notes.statement: Tessier (1976) discussed combinations of several types of clefts and associated malformations, and suggested that the new classification eliminated old confusing terminology and facilitated recording of malformations and treatment planning.
quotes: Combinations of several types of clefts and associated malformations are discussed.
it eliminates the old confusing terminology (based on personal experience and case descriptions in the literature it seems to be complete); it facilitates recording of malformations
